ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left AC power supply is connected between points a and b, and is connected to the primary coil n1 of the first ideal transformer; the secondary coil n2 of the first transformer is on the left side of the middle circuit, and an ideal AC voltmeter V is connected in parallel across n2. The upper end of n2 is connected through resistor R to coil n3 of the second ideal transformer, and the upper and lower ends form the middle loop. The secondary coil n4 of the second transformer on the right is connected with an ideal AC ammeter A2, switch S, and two lamps L1 and L2, where closing S will connect L2 into the right-side load circuit. Reasoning: The power supply provides a constant rms voltage at points a and b, so the voltage across the primary coil n1 of the first ideal transformer is constant. An ideal transformer satisfies the voltage transformation-ratio relation U2/U1 = n2/n1, so the voltage across n2 is fixed as U2 = (n2/n1)Uab. Closing switch S will only change the secondary-side load of the second transformer, thereby changing the currents everywhere and the current distribution through R, n3, and other parts; but it will not change the voltage forcibly applied by the power supply to the primary side of the first transformer, nor will it change the voltage transformation ratio of the ideal transformer. Therefore the reading of the voltmeter connected in parallel across n2 remains unchanged.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit: the source of constant RMS voltage is across the first transformer's primary n1, while V is across its secondary n2; the lamps controlled by S are on the secondary of the second transformer. Apply the ideal-transformer relation to the first transformer: since V_ab is constant, the voltage across n2 is fixed at (n2/n1)V_ab. Closing S may change currents in R, n3/n4, and the lamps, but it does not change the imposed primary voltage or the ideal voltage transformation. Therefore the voltmeter reading across n2 remains unchanged.
